key_insight: Translate structured skeleton data into differentiable, image-like renderings that MLLMs can directly consume, enabling universal, format-agnostic skeleton understanding while preserving end-to-end learnability.
problem_solved: Bridges the modality gap between structured non-visual skeleton representations and multimodal LLMs, avoiding lossy vector compression or brittle discrete tokenization so models can reason about human pose and motion across heterogeneous skeleton formats.
method: Differentiable rendering: convert joints, bones and motion signals into multi-channel, differentiable visual representations that retain spatial and temporal details.
MLLM integration: feed rendered skeleton views to a multimodal LLM (with light adapters or prompt tuning) so the model can perform captioning, QA, and reasoning over poses.
End-to-end training and format-agnostic alignment: optimize rendering and model adapters jointly for robustness across skeleton topologies and improved generalization without bespoke tokenization.
impact: Allows AI/ML practitioners to leverage powerful MLLMs for pose and motion tasks (captioning, action recognition, reasoning, editing) without hand-crafted skeleton encodings, improving interoperability across datasets and real-world systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: skeleton (various formats) → differentiable renderer → MLLM → tasks (caption, QA, action label).
Before vs after: comparison of lossy vector/token approaches vs differentiable rendered input (accuracy/generalization bars).
Example outputs: rendered skeleton images next to MLLM-generated captions/answers and attention/heatmap overlays.
Ablation chart: effect of end-to-end differentiability and adapter training on cross-format performance.
paper_title: Universal Skeleton Understanding via Differentiable Rendering and MLLMs
paper_authors: Ziyi Wang, Peiming Li, Xinshun Wang, Yang Tang, Kai-Kuang Ma
